chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn Ayyoob, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath’ami, from Iss’haq ibn Jareer, from Hijr ibn Za’ida, from Hamran ibn A’yun, who said: I asked Abu Ja’far, saying to him: Are you al-Qa’im?

He said: The messenger of Allah has begotten me, and I am the one sought for blood-avenging, and Allah does whatever He wills. Then I repeated my question to him, so he said: You have known where to go. Your companion is the one with the distended abdomen, then the one with dandruff on his head, the son of the Imams. May Allah have mercy upon so-and-so!

key_terms.الْحَزَّازُ بِرَأِهِ: The one with dandruff on his head
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Rising One / The Awaited One
key_terms.الْمُبْدِحُ الْبَطْنُ: The one with the distended abdomen

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say when asked if he was the al-Qa’im, and who did he identify?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) confirms his identity as the awaited al-Qa’im by highlighting his prophetic lineage and his role in avenging the blood of the Ahl al-Bayt, while emphasizing divine decree. The subsequent identification of a specific companion with distinct physical and social markers illustrates the Shia tradition of recognizing the Imam’s authority through precise, often subtle, signs known to his close followers. This incident underscores the theological balance between the certainty of the Imam’s status and the unfolding of divine will in history.
